summary: The note describes the Open Packaging Conventions (OPC), a container-file technology first created by Microsoft. OPC bundles XML and non-XML files into a single entity, such as an OpenXPS document. The note says OPC-based formats keep the independent file entities intact and produce much smaller files than normal XML use.
one_line: Open Packaging Conventions is a Microsoft-originated container-file technology that bundles XML and non-XML files into one document.
key_facts: The Open Packaging Conventions (OPC) is a container-file technology initially created by Microsoft.
OPC stores a combination of XML and non-XML files that together form a single entity.
An Open XML Paper Specification (OpenXPS) document is given as an example of an entity stored using OPC.
OPC-based file formats leave the independent file entities embedded in the document intact.
OPC-based file formats result in much smaller files compared to normal use of XML.
